text:
Alex: quick sync — thinking about switching pin model from 'hard pin' to a lease/heartbeat model. raises: client resolver, telemetry, and migration. thoughts?
Maria: +1 on leases for safety. main worry: client cache staleness if lease expires mid-query. need clear client-side fallback.
Jun: can we scope leases per-tenant vs global? different SLAs need different durations.
Saad: yes. propose default lease = 24h for hosted, 72h for dedicated, and tenant override flag: `pin.lease_seconds`.
Nikhil: also consider semantic vs content hash id. leases work with either but content-hash lets us guarantee identity; semver helps human ops.
Alex: agree re identity. suggestion: primary identifier = content_hash, optional `alias` = semver/string. client resolver uses alias -> content_hash map with TTL.
Maria: what about automatic minor patch promotion? i.e. alias v1.2 -> content-hash A, then patch -> content-hash B. rollout should allow opt-in auto-swap within lease window.
Jun: opt-in promotions are good, but need a `promotion_policy` enum: `never`, `auto-within-lease`, `auto-if-compat`.
Saad: compatibility needs a small contract field in metadata: `compat_level: "binary-stable" | "api-stable" | "unknown"`. clients can choose to accept only certain levels.
Nikhil: open question: storage overhead for maintaining alias history + telemetry. We should keep a compact index: latest alias -> hash, and optional history pointer stored off the critical path.
Alex: propose schema snippet (very rough):
```json
{
  "pin_id": "string",            // tenant-visible alias
  "content_hash": "sha256:...", // canonical model id
  "lease_seconds": 86400,
  "expires_at": "2026-04-01T12:00:00Z",
  "promotion_policy": "auto-if-compat",
  "compat_level": "api-stable",
  "owner": "team-infra",
  "observability_tags": ["client:mobile", "workload:chat"],
  "deprecation_window_days": 7
}
```
Maria: looks good. add `pin_origin` to indicate manual vs rollout-manager vs import. helps audits.
Saad: and add `grace_policy` for in-flight requests: `serve-stale`, `fail-fast`, `fallback-to-variant`. default to `serve-stale` for UX.
Jun: client resolver algorithm sketch: 1) query local cache; 2) if missing or expired, fetch alias->hash mapping from control plane; 3) validate compat_level if client requires; 4) open request to runtime with chosen hash; 5) if lease absent, log telemetry and use fallback. keep retries bounded.
Nikhil: telemetry fields we need: `pin_resolve_latency_ms`, `pin_fallback_reason`, `resolved_hash`, `lease_age_seconds`. these help alert when pins are drifting.
Alex: agreement check: - default lease semantics as Saad suggested - schema to use content_hash primary + optional alias - promotion_policy + compat_level + grace_policy - client resolver steps as Jun sketched. any objections?
Maria: no objections. action: Alex to draft RFC with the schema + client resolver pseudocode + rollout-manager changes.
Saad: I'll run a small sim to test cache-staleness rates and expected extra control-plane QPS for 24h vs 6h lease. will post numbers tomorrow.
Jun: I'll prototype client resolver with `serve-stale` fallback and a signal to surface when a lease is close to expiry.
Nikhil: I'll add telemetry field defs to the observability spec and map to existing logs/metrics.
deploy-bot: deployed branch `pin-lease-prototype` to staging — 2026-03-19 21:15 UTC :shipit:
Alex: thanks everyone. RFC target EOW.
Maria: tagging @product-review in RFC once ready.
Alex: cool. closing thread for now, will ping when RFC link is up.
